senses.gloss: 1. अ॑प् n. (gen. अप॑स्), work (according to NBD.), RV. i, 151, 4.
2. अ॑प् f. (in Ved. used in sing. and pl., but in the classical language only in pl., आ॑पस्) water
the Waters considered as divinities. ifc. अप् may become अप or ईप, ऊप after इ- and उ- stems respectively.
अप् [cf. Lat. aqua; Goth. ahva, ‘a river’; Old Germ. aha, and affa at the end of compounds; Lith. uppê, ‘a river’; perhaps Lat. amnis, ‘a river’, for apnis cf. also ἀϕρός]
आप् [probably connected with 1. अप्; cf. अप्न; Gk. ἄϕενος, ἀϕνειός; Lat. apiscor, aptus, ops; Old Germ. uoban; Mod. Germ. üben.]
2. आप् (आ-√ आप्) pf. आ॑प, to arrive at, come towards, RV. x, 32, 8.
